title: Practical Security Levels for Side-Channel Resistance
summary: PERSEUS gives tight security bounds in some settings, but its Monte Carlo refinement becomes looser and can saturate; the open task is to set practical levels using real-attack measurement costs.

formal_statement.body: For PERSEUS, determine which practical security levels should be targeted for side-channel resistance when the measurement cost of real attacks is taken into account. The relevant gap arises because PERSEUS can produce a tight security bound, such as $\varepsilon_U \approx 2^{-40}$ for $n=6$ shares and leakage rate $p=2^{-12}$, but its Monte Carlo refinement becomes less tight at higher leakage rates and saturates for high-security circuits, such as RPMult with $n=7$ and $p=2^{-10}$, where it yields the looser interval $2^{-40} \leq \varepsilon \leq 2^{-34}$. The unresolved task is to establish practical target security levels that relate the security parameter $\varepsilon$ to the measurement cost required for a real side-channel attack.

scope.domain: Random-probing side-channel security analysis and calibration of security bounds to real attack costs.
parameters: measurement cost, the cost of a real side-channel attack
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine practical target security levels that relate the security parameter epsilon to the measurement cost required for a real side-channel attack.

progress.summary: The source explicitly presents this as a broader open question arising from PERSEUS's tight bounds in some settings and looser, saturating Monte Carlo refinements in others. It asks how practical side-channel security levels should account for the measurement cost of real attacks.
